title: Midterm Exposure Changes on the Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy
content:
The rated exposures of a Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy, its vehicles, youthful drivers, rental units and watercraft, may be added or removed during the term, and each such change is governed by the clauses below.

## Clauses

1. **Reporting period.** A vehicle, youthful driver, rental unit or watercraft acquired during the term is covered from the day it is acquired only when it is reported no later than the exposure reporting period that starts on the date it was acquired. The exposure reporting period is counted in calendar days from the acquisition date, and a report on the last day is on time. Its length is the tier's exposure reporting period.
2. **Late report.** An exposure reported late is covered only from the report date, and its premium is charged from the report date.
3. **Premium effect.** The premium effect is the annual rate for the exposure multiplied by the calendar days from the exposure's effective date to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent. Removals credit the same way, pro rata from the removal date.
4. **Minimum change.** Changes whose prorated amount is below the tier's minimum premium change are neither billed nor credited.
5. **Tier maximums.** An exposure that would take the umbrella above a tier maximum cannot be added midterm; the umbrella must move to a tier that allows it at renewal.
6. **Underlying insurance.** Each added vehicle, rental unit or watercraft must be scheduled on qualifying underlying insurance, at least at the tier's required limit for its line and with its details exactly as on its declarations page.

## Annual rate for each kind of exposure

| Exposure | Annual rate used in the premium effect |
|---|---|
| Vehicle | The tier's additional vehicle premium |
| Youthful driver | The tier's youthful driver premium |
| Rental unit | The tier's rental unit premium |
| Watercraft | The tier's watercraft premium |

The same correspondence holds on every tier from Larkspur Umbrella 1M to Larkspur Umbrella 10M; the figures are those of the umbrella's own tier.

## The reporting clause restated

| Report date compared with the last day of the period | Covered from | Premium charged from |
|---|---|---|
| On or before the last day | The acquisition date | The acquisition date |
| After the last day | The report date | The report date |

The acquisition date is the date the insured states the exposure was acquired.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical inputs)

**Reporting boundary.** A hypothetical vehicle acquired 10 June on a tier with a 30-day period: the last day of the period is 10 July. Reported on 10 July, it is on time and covered from 10 June. Reported on 11 July, it is late and is covered, and charged, only from 11 July.

**Added exposure.** A hypothetical watercraft on Larkspur Umbrella 3M, annual rate $66.00, effective 1 July, in a 365-day term expiring 1 January: 184 calendar days remain. $66.00 multiplied by 184 and divided by 365 is 33.2712, rounded half-up to $33.27 of additional premium.

**Removed exposure.** A hypothetical rental unit on Larkspur Umbrella 2M, annual rate $48.00, removed 1 October in a 365-day term expiring 1 January: 92 calendar days remain. $48.00 multiplied by 92 and divided by 365 is 12.0986, a credit of $12.10.

**Below the minimum change.** A hypothetical rental unit on Larkspur Umbrella 1M, annual rate $36.00, with 40 calendar days to expiration in a 365-day term: 3.9452, rounded to $3.95. That is below the $5.00 minimum premium change of the 1M tier, so it is neither billed nor credited.

**Tier maximum.** A hypothetical Larkspur Umbrella 2M umbrella already scheduling its maximum of 6 vehicles cannot add a seventh midterm; the seventh vehicle requires a move, at renewal, to a tier whose vehicle maximum allows it.
